vulns.title: is_left_child asserts parent_index against table length, permanently bricking the tree after deletions
vulns.root_cause: is_left_child asserts `parent_index < table::length(&tree.internal_nodes)` before borrowing the internal node. table::length is the COUNT of live internal nodes, not the max live index: internal nodes are keyed by an ever-growing next_internal_node_index, and remove_leaf_by_index deletes internal nodes without renumbering, so live indices become non-contiguous and can exceed the table's current length. A later valid call to is_left_child (reached from next_leaf/previous_leaf/insert_leaf/remove_leaf_by_index) with such an index then trips the assert and aborts, permanently DoS'ing the tree. The check is both wrong and redundant; the fix is to delete the assert.
